Key Research Thinking Patterns: Longitudinal Radiotracer Kinetics for Early Engraftment: Utilizing 18F-FLT PET/CT imaging to quantify cellular proliferation dynamics, enabling the detection of bone marrow recovery up to 20 days prior to clinical signs and revealing fetal-like ontogeny patterns in post-transplant hematopoiesis.

Integer-Valued Transform Coding for Signal Efficiency: Developing novel 2D separable Hirschman transforms that are inherently real and integer-valued to cluster quantized coefficients, thereby improving Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and enabling more efficient M-ary run-length coding in block-based video compression.

Analytic-Signal Backbone Extraction via Mirror Periodic Method: Applying the Mirror Periodic Method (MPM) to approximate analytic-signal backbones for unforced linear harmonic oscillators, effectively mitigating end effects in Hilbert transform computations using short displacement and acceleration signals from single-degree-of-freedom systems.

Multi-Modal Deep Learning for Vertebral Segmentation: Implementing an ensemble of U-Net architectures for CT semantic segmentation combined with PET data fusion to automatically extract Standard Uptake Values (SUV) from medullary cavities, providing a noninvasive alternative to bone marrow aspirates for monitoring transplant outcomes.
Summary Description: Joseph Havlicek is a multidisciplinary researcher bridging biomedical engineering, signal processing, and computer vision. His primary translational focus is the noninvasive monitoring of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), where he leverages 18F-FLT PET/CT imaging and deep learning-based vertebral segmentation to detect early subclinical engraftment. Concurrently, he advances computational mathematics and digital signal processing by developing novel integer-valued transforms for high-efficiency video compression and analytic-signal extraction methods for structural health monitoring. His work integrates clinical oncology with rigorous algorithmic innovation, utilizing platforms like the Gemini TF Time of Flight scanner and U-Net architectures to solve complex problems in medical image analysis and infrared target recognition.
